obstacle: Under current authority (ledger replayed at cutoff 9: committed spent-C and active A/B/C/D holds) no route/start assignment of the six indivisible calls fits worker capacity and cumulative pool allowance at every start. A+B are exactly exhausted, forcing requests 3 and 5 onto B; D forces request-4 to start 12, so requests 1 and 2 must run via AC by start 11, needing 4 C units where only 3 are free until the C3 hold expires at 12.
acceptable_arguments: A+B exhaustion, unique route split, D timing and C shortage at start 11.
Exhaustive enumeration of the 20,736 local combinations against cumulative allowances, with a correct ledger replay.
Any other correct argument tied to the real timed constraints; exact counts, cores or witnesses not required.
acceptable_remedies: Customer approves one more C unit available by start 11.
One more A or B unit.
Early release/shortening of the active C (or other) hold by the customer/ledger owner.
Splitting or reducing the batch, stated as a customer decision.
pitfalls: Greedy first-fit scheduler (starter) also refuses feasible nearby batches.

Treating the timed-out C retry as releasing held-C-late.
Charging only the leaf pool or splitting calls.
unsupported_refusals: Needs live ledger/API credentials; the ledger and rules are supplied offline.
